authors: H. F. Holmes, R. E. Mesmer
title: Aqueous solutions of the alkaline-earth metal chlorides at elevated temperatures. Isopiestic molalities and thermodynamic properties
experimental_method: High-temperature isopiestic method (Oak Ridge facility, in-situ weighing with an electromagnetic balance); MgCl2(aq) against NaCl(aq) as the reference electrolyte, 383-524 K; osmotic coefficients from NaCl osmotic coefficients of Pitzer et al.
uncertainties_stated: not captured in the table pages read; none tabulated per point
quality_remarks: The paper repeats earlier MgCl2 isopiestic work (previous results suggested by others to be in error by several per cent); new values slightly differ. Tables 1 and 2 combine two loadings. Hydrolysis stated to be negligible (pH of samples checked). Osmotic coefficients are stoichiometric, computed by the authors from the molalities; NaCl osmotic coefficients from the Pitzer et al. model. Exact replicate-like entries (e.g. phi 1.0135 twice at 524.12 K with different molalities) kept.
